title: Environmental Vocabulary in Context
grammarNote: Как и в любой области, экологический английский имеет свои устойчивые сочетания. "Reduce emissions" — нельзя "decrease emissions" как замену во всех контекстах. "Protect biodiversity" — нельзя "save biodiversity." Изучай экологическую лексику вместе с её типичными глаголами и предлогами.

grammarTable.subject: REDUCE
grammarTable.example: "Reduce carbon emissions." / "Reduce energy consumption." / "Reduce plastic waste."

grammarTable.subject: PROTECT
grammarTable.example: "Protect endangered species." / "Protect natural habitats." / "Protect the environment."

grammarTable.subject: EMIT
grammarTable.example: "Emit greenhouse gases." / "Emit CO₂ into the atmosphere."

rows.example: "Countries must REDUCE their carbon emissions by 2030." ✅

rows.form: INCREASE: temperatures, sea levels, species diversity
rows.example: "Sea levels are INCREASING at an accelerating rate." ✅
"We must TACKLE climate change now or pay the price later." ✅
"Students are encouraged to CONSERVE energy in dormitories." ✅
"National parks were established to PROTECT natural habitats." ✅
"The government has pledged to RESTORE degraded ecosystems." ✅
"The snow leopard is at risk OF extinction." ✅ (not "at risk for" or "at risk to")
"Deforestation is a threat TO biodiversity." ✅ (not "threat of" in this structure)
"Human activity has an impact ON the environment." ✅ (not "impact to" or "impact in")
"The pollution caused significant damage TO the river ecosystem." ✅
"Industries are responsible FOR 70% of global emissions." ✅
"Deforestation contributes TO climate change." ✅ (not "contribute in")
"Reduce your carbon footprint." = the total carbon emissions caused by your actions.
"Switch to renewable energy sources." = solar, wind, hydroelectric.
"Protect endangered species." = animals or plants at risk of extinction.
"Reduce greenhouse gas emissions." = gases that trap heat in the atmosphere.
"Sustainable development meets present needs without harming the future." ✅
"Central Asia is a biodiversity hotspot." = an area with exceptional species variety.
✅ "TACKLE climate change" or "SLOW DOWN climate change." Climate change is not reduced.
✅ "The environment IS UNDER THREAT" or "AT RISK." "In danger" is less standard here.
✅ "impact ON the environment." Always "ON" for impact collocations.
✅ "contribute TO climate change." Always "TO" after "contribute."

grammarTip:
Экологические коллокации — важнейшие:

REDUCE: emissions, pollution, waste ✅
PROTECT: species, habitats, biodiversity ✅
TACKLE: climate change, environmental issues ✅
CONSERVE: water, energy, resources ✅
EMIT: greenhouse gases, CO₂ ✅
THREATEN: species, ecosystems, habitats ✅

Предлоги:
at risk OF extinction ✅
threat TO biodiversity ✅
impact ON the environment ✅
contribute TO climate change ✅
responsible FOR emissions ✅

💡 Ключевые фразы:
"carbon footprint" / "renewable energy"
"endangered species" / "greenhouse gases"
"sustainable development"

exercises.text: Countries must ___ carbon emissions significantly to meet climate targets.
opts: both reduce and lower are correct
exercises.correct: both reduce and lower are correct
exercises.hint: "REDUCE emissions" ✅ / "LOWER emissions" ✅ — both collocate naturally. "Decrease" is less standard in this context.

exercises.text: Deforestation has a negative impact ___ biodiversity.
exercises.hint: "impact ON the environment/biodiversity." ✅ Always "ON" with "impact." NOT "to" or "in."

exercises.text: "We need to ___ climate change before it becomes irreversible."
exercises.hint: "TACKLE climate change." ✅ = address and deal with it seriously. NOT "reduce climate change" (wrong collocation).

exercises.text: "Species that are ___ may soon become extinct without intervention."
exercises.hint: "ENDANGERED species" = the standard fixed phrase for species at risk of extinction. ✅
"contribute TO climate change/global warming." ✅ Always "TO" after "contribute." ✅

exercises.text: "The factory is ___ for releasing pollutants into the river."
exercises.hint: "responsible FOR releasing..." ✅ "RESPONSIBLE FOR" = the correct phrase for blame/accountability.

exercises.text: "To reduce your ___, choose public transport over private cars."
exercises.hint: "CARBON FOOTPRINT" = the fixed phrase for the carbon emissions produced by your activities. ✅

exercises.text: "The government has pledged to ___ damaged wetland ecosystems."
exercises.hint: "RESTORE damaged ecosystems" = bring them back to their original state. ✅ "Conserve" = protect what exists. "Protect" = prevent further damage. "Restore" = repair. ✅

exercises.text: "Many species are at risk ___ extinction due to habitat loss."
exercises.hint: "at risk OF extinction." ✅ Always "OF" after "at risk." NOT "at risk for" or "at risk to."

exercises.text: "Cars and industry ___ large amounts of greenhouse gases every year."
exercises.hint: "EMIT greenhouse gases." ✅ = release or discharge gases into the atmosphere.

exercises.text: "We should ___ water by taking shorter showers." (use carefully)
exercises.hint: "CONSERVE water" = use it carefully, save it. ✅ "Protect" = defend from harm/threat. Different nuances: conserve = save, protect = defend.

exercises.text: "Climate change ___ many bird species along their migration routes."
exercises.hint: "threatens" / "damages" / "harms" migration routes — all three collocate naturally with climate change. ✅

questions.text: "She has an impact ___ the environment." Correct preposition:

questions.hint: "responsible FOR emissions." ✅ Always "for" after "responsible" for accountability.
"at risk OF extinction." ✅ The preposition is always "of" after "at risk."

questions.text: "We need to ___ carbon emissions to slow warming." (key verb)
"We must ___ climate change urgently." Correct verb:
questions.hint: "TACKLE climate change." ✅ Climate change is tackled, addressed, or slowed — not "reduced."

questions.text: "___ species are those at risk of extinction."
questions.hint: "Threatened" / "Endangered" / "Vulnerable" all describe species at risk — at different conservation risk levels. ✅

questions.text: "Cars ___ large amounts of CO₂." Correct verb:
questions.hint: "emit CO₂" ✅ / "produce CO₂" ✅ / "create CO₂" ✅ — all collocate. "Emit" is the most technical and precise.

questions.text: "To save water in daily life, you should ___ it carefully." (verb)
questions.hint: "CONSERVE water." ✅ = use carefully to save it. "Protect" means defend from harm, not save by careful use.

questions.text: "What is your carbon ___?" (the measure of your emissions)
questions.hint: "carbon FOOTPRINT" = the fixed phrase for measuring your personal or organisational carbon impact. ✅
"threatens" ✅ / "destroys" ✅ / "harms" ✅ — all collocate with species. "Threatens" is most idiomatic in conservation contexts.

questions.text: "The project will ___ degraded ecosystems." (return to original state)
questions.hint: "RESTORE degraded ecosystems." = bring back to original/healthy state. "Conserve" = protect what already exists; "restore" = repair damage. ✅

questions.text: "___ energy means using wind, solar, and water power."
questions.hint: "Renewable energy" ✅ / "clean energy" ✅ / "green energy" ✅ — all are used commonly. "Renewable" is the most technical. ✅

questions.text: "A ___ is a region with exceptional species variety under threat."
questions.hint: "BIODIVERSITY HOTSPOT" = a region with exceptional variety of life AND significant threat. ✅
"responsible FOR releasing pollutants." ✅ = held accountable; bears legal responsibility.
"impact ON the environment" ✅ / "threat TO biodiversity" ✅. Different prepositions for different nouns. ✅
